title: one-column-trial-ledger-amaya
content:
Mini one-column experiment ledger (compact sheet) - quick log for session work.

Format notes: single-line CSV rows, kept intentionally small for copy/paste into quick analysis. Columns: exp_id,date,model,precision,quant,bs (batch size),seq_len,avg_latency_ms,p95_latency_ms,tokens_per_sec,cost_per_1k_tokens_usd,success_rate_pct,notes,next_steps

CSV:
exp-2026-02A,2026-02-20,gptx-small,fp16,none,1,256,12.4,22.1,820,0.42,98,first cold-run after checkpoint restore — KV cold, perf unstable,rerun with warmed kv cache
exp-2026-02B,2026-02-20,gptx-small,fp16,4bit-llm,1,256,10.1,17.3,1005,0.31,97,4-bit quant looks promising for latency/cost, quality quick-check passed on 50 prompts
exp-2026-02C,2026-02-21,gptx-small,fp16,4bit-llm,4,128,9.6,15.9,4300,0.09,95,batching x4 reduces per-token cost; watch p95 regression on long prefixes
exp-2026-02D,2026-02-24,gptx-medium,int8,int8,1,512,34.7,68.2,540,0.78,93,int8 batch=1 high p95 spikes, investigate kernel switch behavior
exp-2026-03-09,berr-ttiny,int8,int8,8,64,6.2,9.8,6200,0.05,99,cheap embedding service variant; stable under burst

Quick observations (scatter notes):
- KV cache warm/unwarm is the dominant factor for single-request latency variance (see 02A vs 02B). Need a short script to pre-warm LRU prefixes for reproducible benchmarks.
- 4-bit quant reduces avg latency ~18-23% vs fp16 for gptx-small across this slice; p95 improvement slightly smaller. Running lightweight prompt-evals to surface quality regressions (done 50 samples so far).
- Batch=4 on small seq_len gives huge throughput gains (tokens/sec), but p95 still sensitive to seq_len spikes — consider dynamic batching cap per route.
- int8 behavior on medium model shows kernel fallback at certain seq lengths (big p95 spikes). Add tracing to capture kernel selection decisions (ops trace + device context).

Handy cost quick math: cost_per_1k_tokens_usd above is a rough mapping from our local pricing sim (includes GPU amortization + energy). Treat as approx.

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Create pre-warm small tool (shell + python) and add to repo bench-scripts/warm_kv.sh — ticket JIRA-4821 assigned to Jules.
- [ ] Expand quality check from 50 -> 500 prompts for 4-bit quant experiments (split A/B). Owner: Amaya. Target: 2026-03-18.
- [ ] Capture kernel selection trace for int8 runs (exp-2026-02D) and attach to PR for infra-team to inspect. Owner: Ravi.

Scratch formulas (for personal calc):
- tokens/sec ~ (batch_size * seq_len) / avg_latency_s
- cost_per_1k = (cost_per_hour_est / 3600) * (1000 / tokens_per_sec) * 3600 / 1000 (quick heur) — use platform cost tool for final

Quick links / references cited in session:
- JIRA-4821 (warm cache script)
- github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/178 (bench harness changes including 4-bit loader)

Notes-to-self style: keep these rows minimal and put final cleaned results in shared drive folder when ready for runbook. This sheet is intentionally ephemeral — snapshot into confluence or dedicated sheet once stable.

End of ledger.
